title: Weed and invader plant management processes

lessons.title: Managing clearing projects at work
lessons.html:
Your workplace role

In this module you take part in managing real weed and invader plant projects: clearing wattle and gums along farm rivers, controlling prickly pear or mesquite on rangeland, keeping silo hardstands and rail sidings free of weeds, and treating weeds around farm buildings and fence lines. You will practise surveying, planning, supervising teams, checking quality and managing follow-up.

Workplace process

  1. Survey and map infestations by species, density and age.
  2. Check the species' status under the NEMBA Alien and Invasive Species lists and the landowner's obligations.
  3. Plan priorities, methods, registered herbicides, team size and follow-up schedule.
  4. Brief and equip the team, including chainsaw operators with full protective gear.
  5. Supervise treatment and check quality daily.
  6. Record work done and herbicide used.
  7. Return for follow-up treatments and monitor regrowth and rehabilitation.

Scenario: wattle along a farm stream

A dairy farmer wants black wattle cleared from 2 km of stream bank. You map dense mature stands, scattered saplings and seedlings. With your mentor you plan felling with immediate cut stump treatment using a product registered for use near water, foliar spraying of saplings away from the water's edge, and hand pulling of seedlings close to the water. Cut material is stacked away from the stream. Follow-up visits are scheduled for the next growing seasons, because wattle seed in the soil will germinate after clearing. The farmer agrees to keep cattle grazing managed so that grass cover can return.

Daily quality checks

Walk the cleared area at the end of each day. Look for untreated stumps (no dye), missed saplings and spray damage to indigenous plants. Correct problems the same day.

lessons.title: Team management, records and evidence
lessons.html:
Leading a clearing team

Clearing teams often work in remote, rough terrain. Good team management keeps them safe and productive.

  • Hold a toolbox talk each morning covering the day's area, hazards, methods and emergency plan.
  • Check PPE and equipment, and confirm that only trained workers use chainsaws.
  • Keep safe distances during felling and agree warning calls.
  • Plan water, shade and breaks to prevent heat stress.
  • Know the nearest medical facility and how to get there; carry a first aid kit. Team leaders need hands-on first aid training from an accredited provider.
  • Watch for snakes, bees and unstable slopes.

Records

RecordContent
Daily work recordArea treated, species, methods, team, hours
Herbicide recordProduct, registration number, quantity, mix, weather
Map updatesTreated, follow-up due, untreated
Fixed-point photosBefore and after, same spot each time
IncidentsInjuries, spills, drift complaints

Portfolio evidence

  • Survey maps and plans you prepared.
  • Daily records and herbicide records.
  • Fixed-point photo series.
  • Mentor observation reports and reflections.

Key points

  • Survey, check legal status, plan, supervise, record and follow up on every project.
  • Use products registered for use near water and keep cut material away from streams.
  • Check daily for untreated stumps, missed plants and damage to indigenous vegetation.
  • Manage team safety: toolbox talks, chainsaw competence, heat stress and first aid.
  • Keep daily, herbicide, map and photo records as evidence.
